svg.title: Rung 5's nerve cord model holds a walking rhythm only while DNg100 fires 10-20 spikes/s, and DNg97 speeds it less than flies'
svg.text: Rung 5's nerve cord: a walking rhythm only in a narrow window
DNg100 drives front-leg rhythms only at drives 300-450, firing about 10-20 spikes/s; driven harder, the network runs away and silences it. No one has recorded DNg100;
walking descending neurons fire about 20-60 spikes/s, most of those recorded steering ones. Adding DNg97, which speeds headless flies' stepping by about half,
speeds the model's rhythm by at most 26%, and the rhythm falls apart.

rect.title: drives that would put DNg100 at 20 spikes/s or more without the network's feedback (the note's mapping), the low end of what walking descending neurons recorded in flies fire; the model's own DNg100 falls silent here
